reason: E1 directly shows that rapid quenching yields an amorphous structure while slow cooling gives crystalline phases, supporting the first two premises. It also states that phosphorus and high entropy enhance glass-forming ability, supporting the third. However, E1 provides no data on crystallization onset temperature or thermal stability of the amorphous phase, leaving the fifth premise unsupported. The fourth premise (diffusion suppression) is a standard mechanism not specifically evidenced in E1.
premises: Rapid quenching (10^5–10^6 K/s) of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 yields an amorphous structure
Slower cooling (52 K/s) of the same alloy produces a complex crystalline microstructure
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance glass-forming ability
Rapid quenching suppresses crystal nucleation and growth by limiting atomic diffusion
Amorphous structure from rapid quenching increases crystallization onset temperature (thermal stability)
